expected_behavior: A queued edit command must only be applied by flushQueue() if the note it targeted is still the same note instance it was queued for -- i.e. the note was not deleted (and not deleted-then-recreated, since a recreated note under a reused id is a different, unrelated note) in the interim. A queued edit to a still-current, never-deleted note must still apply normally.
allowed_repairs: compare cmd.generation to state.noteGeneration[cmd.id] in flushQueue() and skip applying the command when they differ or the note no longer exists
any equivalent validity/generation check performed at flush time before mutating state.notes[cmd.id]
forbidden_repairs: never applying any queued command (trivially avoids the stale-overwrite bug but silently drops legitimate queued edits -- caught by the normal_queued_edit_still_applies regression assertion, not by grader inspection)
removing the queue/offline-batching mechanism (applying edits synchronously instead)
clearing the queue on every deleteNote() call (over-broad -- would also drop queued edits for OTHER, unrelated notes still in the queue)
